scope: 20-table isolated release restore with hosted-shape synthetic Twiddle tables; second restore includes the three archived tables.
checks: The pre-cutover archive and role export restore into a separate cluster and match all 20 tables.
The restored pre-cutover fixture reproduces browser access to private answers, messages and transcripts.
The complete ordered cutover runs on the restored copy and preserves every pre-cutover row in its original columns.
The processing boundary rejects an in-flight membership and stale changes to participation and hosted links.
The same request advances through the earlier private, post and contact phases before handling Circle relationships.
Only the owner can use the exact request and scope. Any hosted disposition needs explicit approval.
A changed Circle revision, disabled guard or unknown cascade stops the operation before data changes.
A late receipt error rolls back the membership, attendance, grant, link and host changes together.
Closed Circles lose the meeting link and remain readable. Other hosts’ meetings, readers’ replies and their RSVPs remain available.
The real Circle detail handler returns a private, readable archive with no meeting link from the restored database.
A second restore preserves the readable archive, the pending member receipt and the exact owner retry.
The actual Auth client hits the synthetic foreign-key refusal while the departing account still has Twiddle links.
Unreviewed dependencies roll back archive activation. Once closed, all three app roles lack table access and owner routines remain private.
Review lists only counts, IDs and a digest. It refuses stored media, minted rows, a woven copy and an AI reply in the same parent-only legacy thread.
The exact review refuses stale approval after a concurrent owner write and detects grant or trigger drift.
A late receipt failure rolls back every change. An exact retry preserves both thread anchors and every unrelated reply, collaborator and reaction.
Changed anchors, a new known copy and a new reference each block identity preparation. The SDK lost-reply check verifies the provider removal after fixture cleanup.
Provider-only erasure clears the attributable post. Wallet-only erasure leaves records with unknown authorship intact.
A second restore preserves the anchor, retained reply, archive access, exact erasure retry and pending public receipt.
